cards.title: Eleven time zones
cards.text: Russia spans 11 time zones. When it is evening in Kaliningrad on the Baltic, it is already the next morning in Kamchatka.

cards.title: The deepest lake
cards.text: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the world's deepest lake at over 1,600 metres and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

cards.title: Lowest land
cards.text: The shore of the Dead Sea, more than 430 metres below sea level, is the lowest point on dry land. Its water is so salty that people float effortlessly.

cards.title: Endless coastline
cards.text: Canada has the longest coastline of any country, over 200,000 km, thanks to its tens of thousands of Arctic islands.

cards.question: Which river is usually ranked the longest in the world?
cards.explanation: The Nile (about 6,650 km) narrowly beats the Amazon in most measurements, though the ranking is debated.

cards.question: Mount Everest sits on the border of Nepal and which other country?
What is the smallest country in the world by area?
Which continent has the most countries?
The Atacama, one of the driest places on Earth, is mainly in which country?

cards.statement: The Sahara is the largest desert in the world.
cards.explanation: Antarctica is larger. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

cards.statement: Australia is wider than the Moon.
cards.explanation: Australia stretches about 4,000 km east to west; the Moon is about 3,474 km across.

cards.statement: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain when measured from base to peak.
cards.explanation: Everest has the highest summit above sea level, but Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller from its base on the ocean floor (over 10,000 m).

cards.statement: Alaska is the westernmost, northernmost and easternmost US state.
cards.explanation: Its Aleutian Islands cross the 180° meridian, so some lie in the Eastern Hemisphere.
La Paz is the highest seat of government in the world.
